messages:
jess-support: Escalation from SigmaApps: SSE chat stream truncates consistently at ~9-12s. Client reconnects, and they see duplicate token/billing events. Topology: Cloudflare -> ALB -> nginx (proxy) -> origin. Customer says ALB emits FIN at same time as truncation. Ticket 98765.

emily-frontend: They provided a minimal repro (curl) — posting here: 

```bash
curl -v -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN>\" \\\"https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream?model=gpt-4o-stream\\\"
```

emily-frontend: Note: their frontend refreshes auth tokens every 10s (short-lived tokens). They said reconnects happen right after a token refresh attempt.

jess-support: Customer pasted their nginx upstream proxy config (redacted): 

```nginx
proxy_buffering on;  # suspect
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection \"\";
proxy_read_timeout 300s;
proxy_send_timeout 300s;
keepalive_timeout 60s;
```

sam-oncall: Interesting — proxy_buffering on can aggregate chunks and delay flushes. ALB default idle timeout is 60s, but truncation at ~10s suggests something else (maybe Cloudflare edge or a client-side reconnect race). Do we have ALB access logs / origin logs around the time?

maria-sre: From origin logs (redacted): 

```
[2025-11-05T18:23:12Z] stream write error: write /var/run/proc: broken pipe
[2025-11-05T18:23:12Z] upstream write failed: connection reset by peer
```

maria-sre: ALB access log line they attached: 

```
2025-11-05T18:23:12.234Z alb request_id=ab12 client_ip=1.2.3.4 target_status=200 elb_status=200 bytes=345 elb_tcp_fin=1
```

emily-frontend: They also saw a single 502 from Cloudflare occasionally when the client retried mid-stream. Hypothesis from customer: token refresh -> client issues new request while old connection half-closed -> upstream/ALB/Cloudflare interplay causes FIN/RST and the client gets a truncated stream then reconnects, causing the server to bill for both partial streams.

sam-oncall: Hypotheses: 
- proxy_buffering on at nginx or buffering at Cloudflare edge is delaying first bytes; when client refresh/requests/heartbeats are missing, ALB/edge decide to close TCP.
- short-lived tokens and client retry logic could be re-issuing identical generation requests without idempotency, causing duplicate billing.

Quick actionable checks: 
1) Reproduce with curl using --no-buffer/-N and include a long-running server stream to observe timing.
2) Turn proxy_buffering off on nginx upstream to ensure flush-on-write.
3) Ensure the service emits periodic SSE keepalive comments (e.g., \":\n\\n\" every 15s).
4) Increase ALB idle timeout to 120s for the target group while debugging.

maria-sre: Also capture a pcap on the ALB target to confirm who sends FIN first. If ALB sends FIN then origin is receiving a FIN mid-write. If origin sends FIN, config/timeout on server may be closing.

emily-frontend: I'll ask the customer to run this instrumented curl and upload logs/pcap: 

```bash
# run from a Linux host behind their CF worker to mimic path
sudo tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/stream.pcap host api.redwood.example &
curl -v -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>\" \\
  \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream?model=gpt-4o-stream\" > /tmp/out.txt
# stop tcpdump after reproducer
```

emily-frontend: Also asked them to try a quick config change: set proxy_buffering off and add `proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade;` just to rule out buffering.

jess-support: For the duplicate billing part, engineering note: recommend idempotency-key header per stream session (if not already) so replays from client retries don't double-bill. Also consider marking short partial generations as non-billable until commit/ack. Filing an internal feature request.

maria-sre: SRE suggestions for debugging window: schedule a 30m window where we can tail origin logs, ALB connections, and capture pcap. I'll need: customer timestamp(s), src IP, and a consent window to run tcpdump. I can also enable increased logging on the target group.

emily-frontend: Customer agreed to try config and run pcap. They will test offloading Cloudflare -> ALB by bypassing CF for a test host to see if Cloudflare edge buffering is factor.

cloudflare-bot: Note: Cloudflare may inject buffering for >= HTTP/2 to HTTP/1 transformations. Check CF worker/transform rules.

sam-oncall: Next steps: 
- Customer to produce pcap + out.txt.
- Try nginx: set proxy_buffering off, add `sendfile off; tcp_nopush on; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` and restart in debug window.
- Increase ALB idle timeout to 120s temporarily.
- Add SSE keepalive every 15s from origin.

jess-support: Thanks — tagging @maria-sre for scheduling. I'll keep SigmaApps updated.

maria-sre: I'll take the debug window once they confirm times. If we see ALB FIN first, escalate to infra to check target group health/idle-probes. If origin FIN, we dig into app-level backpressure and token refresh handling.

jess-support: Closing loop for now; will add logs and pcap when customer uploads. :thumbsup:
